To support this strategy, Bousteard has established partnerships with organizations like SkillsFuture Singapore to upskill small and medium enterprises in the building and engineering sector, helping them build technology capabilities for sustainable development. The company also launched the Bousteard Industrial Fund (BIF) to transform its business model and integrate value-added capabilities across the real estate value chain. Their environmental management system includes ISO 14001:2015 certification for both Bousteard Projects and BIH, with regular recertification demonstrating their commitment to environmental compliance and continuous improvement. strategy_summary:
DBS Bank's decarbonization strategy for 2022 is built around a comprehensive net-zero roadmap with science-based targets and sector-specific approaches. The bank committed to achieving net zero in its financed emissions by 2050, publishing its report 'Our Path to Net Zero - Supporting Asia's Transition to a Low Carbon Economy' which details science-based decarbonization pathways and interim 2030 targets across seven key sectors. To operationalize this commitment, DBS established a dedicated Board Sustainability Committee (BSC) to provide oversight and governance, with the committee reviewing and approving sectoral targets for nine sectors aligned with science-based decarbonization glidepaths. The bank also achieved carbon neutrality in its own operations through a structured four-layer approach: reducing consumption, generating renewable energy, procuring green energy, and purchasing high-quality Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) and carbon credits to offset residual emissions.

The bank has implemented several concrete initiatives to drive decarbonization across its operations and client portfolio. DBS launched a carbon calculator on its LiveBetter platform that tracks customers' carbon footprints based on purchases made with DBS cards, offering them the opportunity to offset their emissions. The bank also developed a suite of sustainable financial products including sustainability-linked loans, green and sustainability-linked bonds, and ESG investment funds to support clients' decarbonization journeys. Additionally, DBS engaged over 1 million customers through its LiveBetter platform and expanded its sustainable product offerings to help clients integrate sustainability into their investment decisions. The bank's approach extends to its institutional banking segment, where it established a new Board Sustainability Committee to sharpen its focus on sustainability and climate-related matters.

To ensure effective implementation, DBS has established robust governance structures with clear accountability. The Board Sustainability Committee receives regular reports from the Group Sustainability Council, chaired by the Chief Sustainability Officer, on progress toward net zero commitments and enhanced sustainability disclosures. The bank also committed to annual reporting on its decarbonization progress in the Sustainability Report, with the BSC reviewing targets periodically. DBS further strengthened its approach by setting specific ESG data coverage targets for two sectors and providing corporate customers with guidance on new financial products to support their decarbonization journeys, demonstrating a comprehensive strategy that integrates operational changes with client-facing solutions to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy.

The company is also implementing a Business Continuity Plan to address climate-related operational disruptions and exploring sugar reduction in products like F&N SEASONS Ice Lemon Tea Zero Sugar.

Supporting these efforts, F&N has established a three-step transition risk assessment process to identify relevant climate drivers and evaluate business implications. The company is actively reducing packaging material usage and waste to minimize environmental impact, while maintaining a focus on renewable energy adoption throughout its business operations. These integrated initiatives form part of F&N's broader sustainability roadmap to meet its 2025 sustainability targets and build resilience against climate-related risks across its value chain.

strategy_summary:
Hong Leong Bank's 2022 decarbonization strategy centers on a clear net zero roadmap with specific targets and financial mechanisms to accelerate the transition to a low carbon economy. The bank has updated its key GHG emissions reduction targets, establishing FY2019 as the baseline year, with a short-term target of 15% to 25% reduction of GHG emissions by 2026, a medium-term target of net zero emissions for operational Scope 1 and 2 by 2030, and a long-term commitment to achieve net zero for all emissions (Scope 1, 2, and 3) by 2050. To operationalize this commitment, the bank has established a comprehensive framework for measuring customers' carbon footprints and is targeting the establishment of a baseline for Scope 3 financing portfolio emissions by the end of FY2024.

The bank is implementing concrete financial initiatives to drive decarbonization, having approved over RM 2.4 billion worth of renewable energy financing in FY2022, which surpassed the 5-year target of RM 500 million. It has also established a new target of additional RM 1.5 billion to finance renewable energy projects by FY2025. To support this financing, the bank launched its Green Bond Framework, which sets guidelines for bond issuance where proceeds are used to finance or refinance green assets and projects meeting specific eligibility criteria. This framework led to the issuance of the bank's first Green Additional Tier 1 ("AT1") Bond worth RM 900 million in April 2022, marking a key milestone as the first issuance of a green AT1 bond by a bank in Malaysia.

Beyond financing, the bank is implementing operational initiatives including a carbon offsetting project with the Malaysian Nature Society to restore degraded forest land in Kuala Selangor Nature Park by planting approximately 50,000 new mangrove trees. The bank also achieved a 6% reduction in Scope 2 emissions compared to FY2021 through its Energy Efficiency & Conservation measures. To support customers' transitions, the bank has developed green financing products across commercial, SME, and retail segments including Renewable Energy Financing, Property Mortgage, and Green Car Financing options, while also building a Greenhouse Gas Emissions calculator to help customers measure their carbon footprints.

strategy_summary:
Hutchison Ports' 2022 decarbonization strategy centers on a science-based approach aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), establishing concrete near-term and long-term emissions reduction targets. The company has officially committed to a 46.2% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2032 from a 2021 baseline and net-zero emissions by 2050. This strategic direction was formalized through the development of a comprehensive net-zero roadmap that integrates equipment electrification, renewable energy adoption, and supply chain emissions management. The strategy represents a significant evolution from previous efforts, with the company moving beyond general commitments to implement structured, measurable initiatives grounded in climate science.

The company executed a three-step decarbonization mapping process in 2022, beginning with emissions baselining through comprehensive Scope 1, 2, and 3 inventories. This data collection formed the foundation for setting science-based targets and developing a tailored decarbonization pathway. Implementation focused on two key components: equipment replacement and renewable energy integration. Hutchison Ports Thailand deployed four remote-controlled and fully electric cranes alongside eight rubber-tyred gantry cranes, while Hutchison Ports FCP (Bahamas) introduced five new hybrid straddle carriers and three quay crane spreaders. The company also initiated a fleet electrification program, with full-scale implementation mandated from 2024, including prohibiting new diesel equipment purchases and transitioning to electric or other green fuel alternatives.

To support these operational changes, Hutchison Ports established a strategic roadmap that incorporates future planning on fleet electrification, renewable energy adoption, and emissions reduction. The company successfully completed its first Scope 3 emissions assessment, recognizing the importance of addressing supply chain emissions. Looking ahead, the strategy includes implementing renewable energy power purchase agreements (REPPA) from 2026 to manage increasing electricity demand from the electrification program. All business units are required to develop emissions reduction targets and action plans aligned with the latest climate science, ensuring a coordinated approach to achieving the company's net-zero ambition by 2050.

strategy_summary:
Jardines' 2022 decarbonization strategy centers on a science-based approach aligned with the 1.5°C pathway, implemented through their 'Building Towards 2030' sustainability framework. The company established a segmented approach recognizing business diversity while maintaining cohesive Group direction, with three core pillars focused on leading climate action, driving responsible consumption, and shaping social inclusion. A key milestone was the publication of their Group Climate Change Policy in June 2022, which explicitly commits to supporting a Just Energy Transition and states the company will not invest in new coal mines or coal-fired power plants. The Climate Action Working Group (CAWG) meets quarterly to drive implementation across businesses and leverage the Group's scale for coordinated action.

The company made significant progress on validating science-based targets in 2022, with Hongkong Land becoming the first business to secure SBTi approval for its 1.5°C-aligned 2030 targets, committing to a 46.2% absolute reduction in scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions and a 22% per m² reduction in carbon intensity for scope 3 by 2030. Hactl, Gammon, and DFI Retail Group have also submitted commitment letters to SBTi for their 1.5°C-aligned targets. Concrete decarbonization initiatives include PT United Tractors' acquisition of renewable energy company Arkora (operating and expanding mini hydropower plants in Indonesia), and the installation of 15.77 MWp of rooftop solar PV projects across Group facilities. Astra is diversifying away from coal, planning to grow non-coal revenue to 88% by 2030.

To support this transition, Jardines completed a comprehensive Group-wide assessment of transition risks in line with TCFD recommendations, engaging colleagues across businesses to develop consistent climate scenarios and risk assessments that are now integrated into business planning. The company is implementing a structured approach with businesses following either the science-based targets path or the TCFD path based on their specific circumstances, while all businesses are developing decarbonization pathways for operational emissions and working to understand and reduce value chain emissions. These efforts are supported by partnerships with organizations like SBTi and a commitment to channel capital toward improving climate resilience and driving innovation in Asian markets.

strategy_summary:
Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust's decarbonization strategy centers on achieving the Mapletree Group's net zero emissions target by 2050 through a structured approach to climate risk management and renewable energy adoption. The company has adopted the TCFD framework to systematically address climate-related risks and opportunities, conducting comprehensive climate risk assessments and scenario analyses across its portfolio. In FY22/23, MPACT conducted its first climate risk assessment using Net Zero (RCP 2.6) and Business-as-usual (RCP 8.5) scenarios, identifying specific transition risks including increased carbon pricing, regulatory mandates, and changing stakeholder expectations, as well as physical risks such as floods, tropical cyclones, and extreme heat. The strategy emphasizes proactive identification of climate vulnerabilities to inform business decisions and investment processes.

The company is implementing concrete renewable energy initiatives to reduce its carbon footprint, with significant progress in solar energy generation. In FY22/23, MPACT increased its installed solar capacity by 600 kWp (from 1,638 kWp to 2,238 kWp) through the addition of 982 solar panel modules at MBC, generating approximately 1,960 MWh of renewable energy. This solar generation translated to an annual reduction of close to 1,389 tonnes of CO2e, equivalent to taking approximately 309 fuel-powered passenger cars off the road for a year. The company has concrete plans to further expand its solar capacity by 1,469 kWp to 3,707 kWp in FY23/24 across MBC and VivoCity properties, with the strategic goal of increasing renewable energy proportion within its energy mix to reduce grid electricity dependency.

To support this transition, MPACT has onboarded a climate risk analysis tool in FY22/23 to enhance the assessment of climate-related risks and investment due diligence processes. This tool systematizes the analysis of both physical and transition risks at the asset level under various climate scenarios. The company is also implementing energy efficiency initiatives across its portfolio, including replacement of motors and fans for air handling units, LED lighting, and upgrading energy-saving equipment. Approximately S$40 million of capital expenditures has been budgeted for FY23/24 for these energy initiatives, demonstrating the company's commitment to integrating decarbonization into its operational framework and investment decisions.

Mewah International’s 2022 decarbonization strategy centers on transitioning operations from fossil fuel dependency to low-carbon energy systems, with a long-term target of achieving a CO₂-free global economy. Additionally, green-enabled energy-efficient technologies were adopted across factories to minimize resource use and GHG emissions, supporting operational sustainability. 

These efforts reflect a phased operational shift toward low-carbon infrastructure, leveraging byproducts like palm waste to create circular energy systems while directly addressing Scope 1 emissions through on-site renewable energy adoption and fuel substitution.

The company also adopted Vehicle planning and optimising solution System I to monitor vehicle travel distances and optimize fuel consumption, demonstrating a data-driven approach to emission reduction.

Looking forward, Mun Siong Engineering plans to install energy-saving lighting, water-saving gadgets, and solar panels at their new office location at 26 Gul Way in the second quarter of 2023. These initiatives, combined with their ongoing focus on energy and water conservation, form a comprehensive approach to reducing their carbon footprint while maintaining operational efficiency. Concurrently, production processes are optimized to run machines at optimum speed for maximum high-quality output and operational hours, with continuous improvements focused on boosting uptime and efficiency through root cause analysis of unplanned stoppages and capacity utilization at lowest unit cost.

In FY2022, the company began aligning its disclosures with TCFD's four core elements—governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets—to enhance transparency and strategic accountability. The company is also strengthening its policy framework to guide management on climate change mitigation, adaptation, and resilience, ensuring consistent implementation across all operational sites. These initiatives collectively integrate operational improvements with formal climate governance, demonstrating a practical pathway to decarbonization through both production optimization and structured risk management.

The company has adopted the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) framework to validate its net-zero emission targets, aiming to align with the 1.5-degree Paris Agreement objective. Recognizing their fabless structure's limitations, Nordic focuses on renewable energy adoption through Guarantees of Origins (GOO) and renewable energy certificates (I-RECs), while leveraging their position as a fabless company to influence suppliers' environmental practices through binding contractual requirements.

The company achieved significant progress in 2022 with a 54.7% reduction in Scope 2 emissions (exceeding their 50% target) and a 21.5% reduction in Scope 3 emissions (against a 20% target). Specific initiatives include a renewable energy program for electricity consumption with a goal to eliminate 100% of emissions by 2025, building on their 2015 introduction of renewable energy in offices. Nordic also implemented product-focused sustainability measures, such as developing cloud services that enable remote industrial control to reduce travel-related emissions, and evaluation kits supporting IoT products with positive climate impact.

For implementation, Nordic established concrete annual targets with metrics tracking, including increasing recycled plastic in device containers from 5% to 6.5% in 2022 (with a 2023 target of 40%). The company uses second-source vital components to mitigate physical climate risks in their supply chain and has integrated climate considerations into R&D investments. In 2023, Nordic plans to validate new climate targets with SBTi, reduce air travel emissions by 50% compared to 2019, and further reduce Scope 2 emissions by 50% compared to 2022, demonstrating a structured, target-driven approach to decarbonization.

strategy_summary:
Nufarm's decarbonization strategy in 2022 centers on a dual approach: developing renewable bioenergy platforms and implementing targeted emissions reduction measures at key manufacturing sites. The company is building a bioenergy platform through the acquisition of GranBio's energy cane breeding and commercial assets, which aims to fundamentally improve energy output through innovation in bioenergy cane. This includes the independently certified Nuseed Carinata, which the US Environmental Protection Agency approved as a renewable fuel feedstock under the Renewable Fuel Standard program. In FY22, Nufarm planted over 41,000 hectares of Nuseed Carinata in Latin American and US markets, with plans to expand to more than 80,000 hectares in 2023, validating its low greenhouse gas emission potential.

For operational emissions, the company prioritized its two largest emitting sites - Pipe Road in Australia (contributing more than 50% of global manufacturing emissions) and Wyke in the UK - which together account for over 80% of reported emissions. At Pipe Road, Nufarm is establishing a power purchase agreement to supply electricity and using large-scale generation certificates to offset scope 2 emissions. The company completed a decarbonization strategy for this site, identifying energy efficiency and electrification opportunities to pursue over the next few years. At Wyke, the company is progressively replacing steam heat tracing with electric heat tracing, which will improve energy efficiency of the combined heat and power plant. Additionally, Nufarm undertook a feasibility study into reusing hydrogen generated from the chlorine process to contribute to emissions reduction.

The company has set a clear target to reduce scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions from manufacturing sites by 30% by 2030. While acknowledging that transitioning to renewable energy is not currently economical at these sites, Nufarm anticipates this situation will change in the late 2020s or early 2030s and is pursuing interim measures to reduce emissions while continuing to investigate alternative means to accelerate emissions reduction. The strategy demonstrates a phased approach that combines immediate operational improvements with longer-term bioenergy development to address both scope 1 and 2 emissions.

strategy_summary:
Olam's decarbonization strategy for 2022 centers on reducing greenhouse gas emissions through targeted energy consumption reduction and comprehensive emissions accounting, with particular emphasis on supply chain emissions. The company recognizes that Scope 3 (supply chain) emissions account for over 90% of its total GHG footprint, making this a critical focus area for its decarbonization efforts. Olam is committed to ensuring emissions from operations do not grow at the same pace as business expansion and is developing group-specific targets to align with a 1.5°C climate pathway through dedicated sustainability strategies for key product lines including Cocoa Compass, Coffee LENS, Cashew Trail, Hazelnut Trail, and Almond Trail. The company has established a clear emissions reduction approach focused on reducing energy consumption, particularly fossil fuel use, as a primary lever for lowering greenhouse gas emissions across its operations.

To implement this strategy, Olam has expanded its GHG accounting to include freight business for improved inventory completeness and applied the latest emission factors from Ecoinvent (version 3.9) to ensure accurate calculations. The company has also implemented specific accounting treatments for biogenic carbon emissions, categorizing 5.95 MM tCO2e from biogenic sources appropriately under 'biogenic carbon' in line with Greenhouse Gas Protocol guidance. In 2022, Olam reported comprehensive Scope 3 emissions at 89.5 MMT CO2e, including more complete GHG inventory for packaged foods business (OGA) and dairy trading business (ofi), demonstrating its commitment to transparency and measurement accuracy. The company's approach to Scope 3 emissions includes more complete reporting across multiple categories such as purchased goods and services, transport and distribution, and downstream leased assets.

Olam's decarbonization strategy is supported by its long-term participation in the Carbon Disclosure Project since 2011, providing external verification of its emissions reporting. The company utilizes the GHG Protocol Suite of Standards with an operational control approach, reflecting its degree of influence and control over direct emission sources. While the strategy acknowledges the significant contribution of agriculture to global emissions (up to 8.5% directly, plus 14.5% from land use change), Olam focuses its efforts on reducing emissions within its operational boundaries through these structured initiatives. The company continues to develop specific group targets and strategies to implement its decarbonization approach across its diverse business operations.

strategy_summary:
Prudential's decarbonization strategy for 2022 centers on a multi-faceted approach targeting both investment portfolio emissions and operational carbon footprint while prioritizing just and inclusive transitions in emerging markets. The company has established concrete metrics and timelines, including a long-term net-zero target for 2050 and a specific commitment to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of its investment portfolio by 25% by 2025 against a 2019 baseline. By the end of 2022, they had already achieved a 43% reduction in WACI and substantially completed (97%) their divestment from coal bonds, with full divestment from coal equities. Their operational strategy includes a target to reduce emissions intensity by 25% from a 2016 baseline by 2030, with progress demonstrated by achieving 1.21 tCO2e/FTE in 2022 against a 2030 target of 1.65 tCO2e/FTE.

The company published its first Climate Transition Plan in 2022, which outlines their decarbonization pathway and serves as a key strategic document. A cornerstone initiative under this plan is the Emerging Markets Transition Investment (EMTI) project, which Prudential leads within the Net Zero Asset Owner Alliance (NZAOA). This project includes specific actions such as organizing public webinars and publishing a 'Code Red' discussion paper calling for urgent action on emerging markets transition investment. Complementing this, Prudential published a 'Just and Inclusive Transition' paper that emphasizes the social dimensions of climate transition, particularly in regions where they operate.

To support implementation, Prudential has restructured its governance framework by transferring ESG responsibilities to the Group Risk Committee (GRC) in July 2022 and holding dedicated climate deep dive sessions with the Board. The company actively engages with companies responsible for 65% of absolute emissions in their portfolio (a target fully met in 2022) and participates in international standard-setting bodies including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). They also support blended finance mechanisms such as Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JETPs) in Vietnam and the Energy Transition Mechanism (ETM) in Indonesia, demonstrating their commitment to financing just transitions in emerging markets.

strategy_summary:
Sasseur REIT’s 2022 decarbonization strategy centers on integrating climate risk and opportunity assessment into core business operations, guided by TCFD recommendations and scenario analysis. The company prioritized establishing foundational climate governance and data systems, including the creation of a Sustainability Committee (SC) in July 2022 to strengthen climate-related governance. A key focus was conducting climate scenario analysis to evaluate physical risks (e.g., floods, heatwaves) and transition risks (e.g., policy shifts, market trends) using frameworks from the IPCC (RCP8.5, RCP2.6) and IEA (STEPS, NZE), which informed risk mitigation and opportunity identification. The company also initiated its decarbonization journey by establishing a greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory to monitor Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, as detailed in its Sustainability Report.

Specific 2022 initiatives included assessing renewable energy opportunities through cost-saving analyses of solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power, comparing Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) across scenarios to identify viable pathways. For instance, the company explored deploying on-site PV systems and Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for Sasseur (Kunming) Outlets, leveraging China’s renewable energy policies and declining LCOE trends. Concurrently, Sasseur REIT engaged tenants through face-to-face ESG dialogues to promote energy and water conservation, reduce waste, and encourage recycling, recognizing tenant behavior as critical to emissions reduction. These efforts were complemented by ongoing assessments of transition risks, such as potential revenue loss from shifting tenant preferences toward zero-carbon buildings, ensuring strategic alignment with market dynamics.

The company is specifically targeting improvements in energy efficiency and reduction of affiliated wastage, with particular attention to optimizing air-conditioning system temperatures.

Supporting these initiatives, SBS Transit engages stakeholders through quarterly briefings, email communications, and monthly energy performance trending materials to maintain transparency. The structured approach combines continuous monitoring, targeted efficiency improvements, and renewable energy adoption to systematically reduce the company's carbon footprint while maintaining reliable public transportation services. The company explicitly supports the Carbon Offset Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) as the primary global Market-Based Measure to achieve carbon-neutral growth beyond 2020, and is actively engaged in meeting CORSIA's Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) system requirements. SIA recognizes the critical importance of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) in the industry's transition toward a sustainable and low-carbon economy, and works closely with the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS), International Air Transport Association (IATA), and industry partners to advocate for policies that encourage large-scale SAF adoption. The airline acknowledges the evolving nature of climate change issues and associated transition risks, including potential market distortions from uncoordinated climate policies.

To address these challenges, SIA actively engages with stakeholders to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and environmental footprint. The company participates in industry forums such as the Board's Customer Experience, Technology and Sustainability Committee (CETSC) and the Sustainability Steering Committee (SSC), which involve senior management and relevant business units in climate-related risk assessment and mitigation. SIA conducts annual Group-wide Risk Management Review exercises involving stakeholder-driven risk assessments, recognizing that both transition and physical risks could impact financial, operational, and strategic aspects of the business.

While SIA demonstrates awareness of the need for decarbonization and participates in industry-wide initiatives, the strategy outlined in the 2021/22 sustainability report focuses primarily on risk management and supporting regulatory frameworks rather than detailing specific internal targets or implementation timelines for emissions reduction. The company also conducts climate risk assessments and scenario analyses in line with Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations, with plans to make required disclosures from FY2022/23 based on upcoming Singapore Exchange (SGX) requirements.

strategy_summary:
ThaiBev's decarbonization strategy for 2022 centers on a three-pillar approach that integrates climate risks and opportunities into its core business operations. The company has established a clear net-zero target for Scopes 1 and 2 emissions by 2040, with an interim target of 50% reduction in these emissions by 2030 compared to 2019 levels. Additionally, ThaiBev aims for 50% renewable energy usage by 2030 and net-zero Scope 3 emissions by 2050. This strategic framework is embedded within ThaiBev's 'Enabling Sustainable Growth' strategy, which sets quantifiable targets to drive sustainable development and resilience across its business while protecting the environment and supporting local communities. The company's vision focuses on improving climate resilience and supporting a low-carbon economy in line with the 1.5-2°C pathway, with an ambition to adapt to and mitigate climate change while enhancing value creation for its business and connected communities.

The company is actively working toward ISO 14001:2015 certification by FY 2023, which will formalize their environmental management system requirements. SETSCO, a subsidiary, has already achieved ISO 50001 certification for its Energy Management System and is an Energy Efficiency National Partner (EENP) with Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA).

The company's decarbonization efforts are supported by strategic partnerships and certifications that provide external validation and guidance. Both VICOM and SETSCO attained Eco-Office certifications from the Singapore Environment Council in 2022, with VICOM receiving the Champion award and SETSCO the Elite award. These certifications complement their alignment with ComfortDelGro Group's Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi) commitment. SETSCO's Bukit Batok building is also Green Mark Certified by Singapore's Building and Construction Authority, demonstrating their commitment to sustainable infrastructure. Through these interconnected initiatives and certifications, VICOM is building a systematic approach to emissions management that supports both their operational needs and Singapore's national climate ambitions.

strategy_summary:
Wilmar International's decarbonization strategy for 2022 centers on a comprehensive approach targeting both operational emissions and supply chain impacts. The company has completed the mapping of its Scope 3 GHG emissions for the baseline year 2020, which will inform priority areas for their climate roadmap. A key element of their strategy is developing comprehensive targets consistent with a 1.5-degree Celsius pathway and aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), which will be linked to energy and water efficiency programs across their operations.

The company has implemented several concrete initiatives to reduce operational emissions. They have deployed 66.2 MWp of rooftop solar panels across their operations with an additional 105.8 MWp planned for global rollout. In sugar operations, they've developed an Energy and GHG Reduction Pathway that includes using biomass for renewable electricity generation and collecting biogas - resulting in 11.16 million Nm³ of biogas collected in 2022, representing a total reduction of 8,558 MT of coal and 0.2 million tCO₂e. Their Kunming, China refinery has achieved carbon neutrality certification, while in Australia and New Zealand, they've invested in renewable energy certificates to offset energy usage. The company has also transitioned their vehicle fleet, with 139 vehicles across Australia and New Zealand (38% increase from previous year), including 22% electric or hybrid vehicles, and implemented route optimization that reduced distance travelled by 32%.

To address Scope 3 emissions, Wilmar is developing a Palm Oil Sectoral Roadmap to accelerate supply chain action and has partnered with the South East Asia Rainforest Research Partnership (SEARPP). They've implemented a program to ensure all suppliers' palm oil volumes are in the 'delivering' category of the NDPE IRF by 2025. The company is working with industry peers on NDPE commitments and has established monitoring systems to track progress on conservation and climate initiatives, demonstrating a holistic approach to decarbonization across their value chain.
